technical_issues.issue: The report says RAAN indicates the location of the launch facility. RAAN specifies the inertial orientation of the ascending node; it is not determined by launch-site location alone, and the stated value is not justified by a launch-time or orbit-plane analysis.

A sun-synchronous orbit does not inherently provide continuous sunlight to the spacecraft. Eclipse exposure depends on the orbit's local time of node and seasonal geometry; the report does not specify these or establish continuous illumination.

The report selects 600 km altitude and discusses a 250 km reef width but supplies no sensor field of view, swath, ground resolution, spectral capability, or target-access analysis to show that fluid-lensing observations are feasible or that useful reef coverage is achieved.
The access table repeats the 5 February 13:00 access as entries 14 and 15. This duplicate may inflate the stated access count and contributes to the reported statistics.

The drag-sail disposal concept has no sail sizing, decay-time estimate, or compliance demonstration. A passive drag sail is not an orbital manoeuvre, so the report's description of EOL as the mission's orbital manoeuvre is inconsistent.

Vega E is described as unbuilt and its proposed schedule is speculative, yet it is selected without demonstrating a confirmed launch opportunity, rideshare availability, or delivery to the required orbit.

overall: A coherent preliminary mission concept is presented with a plausible SSO and Australian ground facility, supported by STK screenshots and access results. Important design claims remain unverified, including reef imaging performance, launch compatibility, and EOL decay. Operator/customer roles, figure labelling, software files, and referencing also need improvement.

feedback.summary: You present a coherent Australian reef-monitoring concept, with a proposed spacecraft, orbit, launch option, ground facility and mission duration. The STK access results and images provide useful design evidence. To strengthen the report, verify key technical claims, clarify who operates the spacecraft and who uses its data, and improve the support and presentation of your conclusions.
next_steps: In the Introduction, identify the spacecraft operator separately from government and scientific customers, and strengthen the mission rationale with consistent, appropriate sources.

In Mission Design, validate the launch opportunity and delivery orbit; justify RAAN using orbit-plane and launch-time analysis; demonstrate reef-imaging capability and coverage; correct the duplicated access entry; and quantify drag-sail disposal time. Include the relevant software files.

In the Conclusion, synthesize what your evidence establishes and acknowledge unresolved design limits. Number and title Images 1–5 consistently, check writing and formatting, and ensure in-text citations match a suitable reference list.
